terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A one-piece moulding: nothing opens, turns or swings, nothing attaches, so one root pivot and zero sockets. A hundred of these round a beer garden is the design case, so the single draw call is the design constraint. Cream-white polypropylene scuffed grey, a rust-yellow stain at the top of the back, black foot caps; stacked in towers when not in use.

reasoning: ONE component on ONE material -- ONE draw call of two: the seat pan (a flattened 20-segment cylinder), the apron and four legs (tapered sweeps), the lower back band, six fan ribs with two slot fillers and a three-piece top rail (five wedge slots), two arms plunging into the front legs over open flanks (v4), the stain, 36 perforation marks and eight dots, four foot caps, all merged.
One material: cream polypropylene at 0.50 as a vertex colour on a WHITE material, the apron a shade lower, perforations mid-grey, foot caps dark, and a 256 px grime canvas after construction.
No repetition system at one draw call: six ribs, the rail and 36 perforation marks are boxes inside the single merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one declared box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is a solid shell back pierced by five narrow wedge slots under a rounded top rail (the plate; v1's five free slats with wide gaps read as a wooden chair), closed flanks under the arms, arms that run straight down into the front legs, a dished seat with the radial perforation pattern, and fin legs tapering to dark caps. A slatted seat or straight vertical back would be a different chair; the perforation pattern is what says monobloc rather than garden bench.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: a solid shell back with five wedge slots under a rounded top rail, over a solid band
arms running down into the front legs
dished seat inside a deep apron
radial perforation pattern on the seat
tapered fin legs with dark caps
grey scuffs and a rust stain

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The perforations are recessed marks, not holes: 36 thin mid-grey boxes 0.5 mm proud of the seat. Real slots would cost triangles and the hole gate, and at prop distance a dark recess and a hole read alike; declared as a substitution.
The arm drops straight into the front leg as one panel (the plate shows a continuous curve); a first build with a separate arm post and a leg beside it read as a wooden chair.
The lower back is solid from the seat to arm height and the slots are closed by a top rail: the plate shows the wedge slots stopping short of the rounded top edge and closing at the bottom.
The declared plan was corrected 0.55 -> 0.59 x 0.57 on the proxy before building (arithmetic in envelopeDerivation).
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.59 x 0.80 x 0.57 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: the chair envelope. The shipped compound is DERIVED from the geometry by scripts/derive-colliders.mjs.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: The perforations are recessed marks, not holes: 36 thin mid-grey boxes 0.5 mm proud of the seat. Real slots would cost triangles and the hole gate, and at prop distance a dark recess and a hole read alike; declared as a substitution.
The arm drops straight into the front leg as one panel (the plate shows a continuous curve); a first build with a separate arm post and a leg beside it read as a wooden chair.
The lower back is solid from the seat to arm height and the slots are closed by a top rail: the plate shows the wedge slots stopping short of the rounded top edge and closing at the bottom.
The declared plan was corrected 0.55 -> 0.59 x 0.57 on the proxy before building (arithmetic in envelopeDerivation).

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at ground, +Y up, +Z the FRONT face (the face the plate shows).

silhouette.description: A 0.59 m wide moulding: seat pan topping at 0.45 inside a 0.47 x 0.41 apron from 0.36; a 0.43 wide lower back band from 0.44 to 0.56 leaning 30 degrees, then six ribs 0.052 (outer 0.075) wide leaning 14 degrees from 0.545 to 0.775 on centres fanning 0.068 -> 0.074 (slots 16 -> 22 mm, the outer two filled over their lower half), under a 0.50 wide top rail whose ends drop 6 degrees, topping at 0.806; arms as moulded elliptical sweeps 0.085 x 0.034 at 0.616 from z -0.185 to +0.155, curving up into the outer ribs at the back and plunging down into the tops of the front legs with the flank under each arm open (v4); four fin legs 0.040 x 0.060 at the foot widening to 0.066 x 0.090 at 0.53 (front) and 0.056 x 0.120 (rear), front feet at z +0.23 and rear at -0.195.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x +-0.295 at the arms, y 0 to 0.806 at the top rail, z -0.298 at the top of the back to +0.29 at the front legs. v2 lays every z station out from the proxy BACK PLANE at z -0.285: back top 0-0.06 m from it, rear feet 0.06-0.12 m (centre -0.195; v1 stood them 0.15 m further forward), arms 0.10-0.505 m, seat 0.135-0.55 m, front feet centred 0.515 m. Declared 0.55 x 0.80 x 0.55 (w/h = d/h 0.6875). The Meshy proxy of the plate measures bbox 1.404 x 1.899 x 1.351, w/h 0.739 and d/h 0.712 -- inside tolerance but 7% wider -- so with height as the trustworthy axis (a monobloc armchair is 0.78-0.82 m) the plan is 0.80 x 0.739 = 0.59 by 0.80 x 0.712 = 0.57, and the declaration was corrected to match. Stations off the proxy (occupancy, 50 rows of H, 80 columns of W): back slats rows 0.82-0.98 across 0.71 W with gaps at columns 34 and 45, their z range from 0.18 H at 0.82 to 0.04 H at 0.98 (read as TWO slopes in v2: the lower band rows 0.48-0.58 at ~30 degrees, the panel rows 0.58-0.98 at ~14, so the top stays inside D); arms rows 0.72-0.80 the full width, 0.40 m long, 0.09 wide each; seat rows 0.48-0.56 (top 0.45 m) over 0.84 W by z 0.17-0.69 H; an apron rows 0.40-0.46; a solid lower back rows 0.58-0.70; front legs at x +-0.44 W and z 0.60 H, rear legs at z 0.10 H, both as fins whose webs (columns 8-20) taper from row 0.46 to 0.00.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bbox 1.404 x 1.899 x 1.351, w/h 0.739 and d/h 0.712, which widened the declared plan 7%. Every station above is the proxy band table in fractions of H; the plate settled the back's construction (a solid shell with five wedge slots, which the proxy renders as a near-solid panel with gaps only at columns 34 and 45 -- consistent), the perforation pattern and the arm section, which the 20 mm voxel fuses. v2 read the proxy's z stations from its back plane: rear feet 0.075 H from it, back top 0.007 H, arms 0.12-0.62 H, seat 0.17-0.69 H; top-band width 0.39-0.46 m against v1's 0.46-0.58 fan.

viewEvidence.note: NOT OBSERVED. The back of the slats and the rear legs are hidden; built as the mirror of the front with the rear fins narrower, confidence 0.8.

componentTree.name: Moulded armchair
componentTree.topologyRationale: One merge of a flattened cylinder, two elliptical arm sweeps, five tapered sweeps, forty-odd boxes and eight discs on one material: ONE draw call, because the design case is a hundred of them.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Seat pan r 0.228 x 0.86 in z, 0.020 thick topping at 0.45; apron 0.42 x 0.36 -> 0.47 x 0.41 from 0.36 to 0.445; back band 0.43 wide from 0.44 to 0.56 leaning 30 degrees; six ribs 0.052/0.075 wide, 0.022 thick, from 0.545 to 0.775 leaning 14 degrees on centres 0.068 -> 0.074, two 0.03 x 0.11 fillers closing the outer slots' lower half, a top rail 0.20 + 2 x 0.15 wide, 0.032 x 0.026, ends dropped 6 degrees; arms as ONE moulded station sweep each (v3, owner review): a flat elliptical section 0.085 x 0.034 running level at 0.616 from z -0.185 to +0.155, rising in an eased curve into the outer rib (0.060 wide, 20 mm inboard, buried at 0.70 / z -0.262) and dipping in a steeper second curve to 0.505 at z +0.242 straight into the top of the front leg (v4, owner review: no side web and no front fin, the flank under the arm is open); front legs 0.040 x 0.060 -> 0.066 x 0.090 from the foot to 0.53 and rear legs -> 0.056 x 0.120, 0.368 tall, at z +0.23 / -0.195; caps 0.042 x 0.014 x 0.062.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The seat pan sits inside the apron's rim as interpenetrating solids; the leg tops run 20 mm up into the apron; the arm sweeps run 22 mm into the outer ribs and end inside the front legs' tops as interpenetrating solids; ribs run 15 mm into the band's top and 12 mm into the rail as interpenetrating solids; perforations, stain and caps are proud by their own thickness. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 0.45 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Cream as a vertex colour on a white material with a grime canvas; apron, perforations, caps and stain as vertex colours.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box: the chair envelope. The shipped compound is DERIVED from the geometry by scripts/derive-colliders.mjs.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/back.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: the arms, the seat and the top of the back
localOverrides.evidence: crops/arm.png -- grey scuff marks along the arm; crops/back.png -- a rust-yellow stain at the top of the left slat. Carried as the grime canvas and a proud stain box.

evidence: Measured on the plate: lit plastic #f3f2ef / #fafaf9 (242-250), back slats #d8d5bf (211), legs in shade #d0c5a7 (197), arm shade #ece0bf (224); analyze_texture meanLum 199 sat 0.16 on the back and 180 with specularFraction 0.45 on the arm; extract_pbr_evidence palette #DAD3B1 #454034 #EDE4C2 #CEC295 #AAA483 at confidence 0.86 on both crops.

Textureless as DECLARED: cream 0xefeadc as a vertex colour, apron 0xd9d3c2, perforations 0x8f8474 (luma 132 at saturation 0.19 -- clear of the gate's backdrop band), foot caps 0x6a5a4a (black in the plate, lifted on chroma), the stain 0xd9c9a2, and a 256 px grime canvas after construction.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.

Owner review (v4, 2026-09-03): "geometry under the armrests should be removed; blocks sticking out of the legs and the front join the arms at an awkward angle; make the arms join the legs smoothly". The 20 mm side webs and the front fin frusta are gone; each front leg is one tapered fin from the foot to 0.53 (0.066 x 0.090 at the top) and the arm's end curve is steepened to plunge into that top (nose 0.505 at z +0.242, its crown 15 mm above the leg top).

The back rebuilt to the plate as a solid shell with five wedge slots (six fanned ribs, two fillers, a three-piece rounded rail) in place of five free slats; open windows under the arms closed with 20 mm side webs; arm fronts made tapering frusta into the legs.

Owner review (v3): the flat box arms replaced by one moulded elliptical station sweep per side (17 stations, 12 segments) that rises in an eased curve 22 mm into the outer back rib, runs level, and dips into the front leg fin -- smooth curves, connected to the back.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90. 1736/2000 triangles, 1/2 draw calls, 1/2 materials, 1/4 unique geometries, one canvas. Turntable with --allow-holes: the enclosed background is the five wedge slots, real openings. v4: with the flanks under the arms open, the 90/270 frames carry one real enclosed opening each (hole-check thickest 62.8 px, the space between arm, seat, leg and back), so --allow-holes is now justified by that measured opening rather than by the slot rims alone; the 90/270 silhouette ratios read 0.733 against 0.90 with the webs, because the flank area is gone.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: plastic only: 1 of 2; every tone is a vertex colour on it.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1736 of 2000: two 17-station 12-segment arm sweeps (792), a 20-segment flattened cylinder, seven tapered sweeps, forty-nine boxes and eight 6-segment discs.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A flattened cylinder for the seat pan; tapered sweeps (frusta) for the apron and legs; elliptical station tubes (tubeAlong) for the arms; rotated boxes for the band, ribs, rail, perforations, stain and caps; small discs for the dot perforations.
No InstancedMesh at one draw call. In a scene the HOST instances the chair -- by the hundred.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
The material is declared textureless. One 256 px grime canvas after construction, 0.25 MB; the factory built in under 50 ms.

risks.description: The seat pattern is recessed marks, not openings.
risks.mitigation: Declared as a substitution; 36 proud mid-grey boxes and discs read as slots at prop distance.

risks.description: The five wedge slots in the back enclose backdrop from the front and rear; the flanks are closed in v2.
risks.mitigation: Real openings: --allow-holes on the holeviz and _holecc measurements.

risks.description: A monobloc's arm is one curved flow into the leg; boxes and sweeps can read as a wooden chair.
risks.mitigation: The first build did, and v2's flat box arm stopped 37 mm short of the ribs (owner review: arms hanging in the air, not moulded). v3 sweeps each arm as one elliptical station tube that rises into the outer rib and dips into the front fin, so the arm, the back and the leg read as one moulding.
